entries.headline: Fire near Ras Tanura export terminal; Houthis claim new strikes on pipeline, Riyadh airport
changes: Saudi authorities contained a fire near Ras Tanura, Aramco's largest crude export terminal, after an attack early Oct 27; Bloomberg reported the extent of the damage was unclear and no group had claimed responsibility.

The Houthis said Oct 26 they struck pumping stations on the East-West pipeline and fired a missile at Riyadh's airport hours after it reopened; Saudi Arabia and Aramco have not confirmed either claim.
Brent eased to about $114.88 and WTI to $101.21 on 27 Oct after Monday's profit-taking, while TTF (~€94.67) and JKM LNG ($32.20) both set fresh 2026 highs.

entries.headline: Hormuz traffic falls to a third of normal; Houthi missiles again target Yanbu and Riyadh
changes: JMIC: Strait of Hormuz transits fell to about 101 ships over Oct 22-24, roughly a quarter of the ~138/day pre-war average, with about 492 vessels now waiting outside the strait.
Bab el-Mandeb traffic also fell, to about 58 transits over the same three days against a baseline near 61/day.

Saudi-led coalition air defenses intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at the Yanbu area and Taif on Oct 24, then Riyadh and a Khamis Mushait air base on Oct 25; no damage to Aramco facilities was reported.
Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, closed since a deadly Houthi strike on Oct 10, broadly reopened Oct 25.

entries.headline: UAE oil spill, record tanker rates, and Iran's disputed Hormuz damage claim
changes: An oil leak off the UAE coast forced beach closures in Ras Al Khaimah, Sharjah and Umm Al Quwain.
The IEA says shipping crude from the Gulf to Asia now costs over $37/barrel, more than five times pre-war levels.
Record tanker rates are pushing US crude exports to Asia toward a seven-year low.
Saudi Aramco is seeking overseas storage deals abroad to diversify away from Gulf supply risk.
Iran claimed seven vessels were struck or mined near Hormuz on Oct 21; Trump called it faked, and maritime monitors found no substantiation.

entries.headline: Brent settles at highest since April on reports of planned post-midterm Iran strikes
changes: Brent crude settled at $116.72/bbl on Oct 23, its highest close since April, as markets priced in reports the US and Israel are planning renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms.
QatarEnergy signed a long-term deal for up to 4 million tonnes a year of US LNG from Cheniere, running 2031-2054, to offset capacity lost at its war-damaged Ras Laffan plant.
The US Treasury sanctioned a Greek law firm, two shipping agents and nine vessels for helping move Iranian oil, petrochemicals and steel past sanctions.
A new estimate puts Iran's floating oil stockpile, built up before the US blockade, down to about 29 million barrels from 90 million in mid-July and close to exhausted.
Pump prices refreshed from official US, EU and UK feeds.

entries.headline: Brent hits five-month high after fatal drone strike near Saudi oilfield; US pulls diplomats
changes: A Houthi drone strike near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield on Oct 21 killed two contractors and injured two more; Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said oilfield operations were unaffected.
The US ordered non-emergency diplomats and their families to leave Saudi Arabia the same day, citing escalating Houthi attacks on civilian targets.
Brent crude rose to about $114.55/bbl, its highest since May, up roughly 8% on the week; TTF and JKM gas also set fresh 2026 highs.
Pump prices refreshed from official US, EU and UK feeds.

entries.headline: Ship attacks near the Arabian Peninsula more than double in October despite recovering oil flows
changes: UKMTO has recorded 32 attacks on commercial vessels around the Arabian Peninsula so far in October, versus 16 for all of September, even as Middle East oil flows hold near pre-war levels on bypass routes.
Suez Canal container traffic is back above half of 2023 (pre-crisis) levels for the first time since the Houthi campaign began, per BIMCO/Clarksons data.

Brent crude climbed to a fresh five-month high near $112/bbl on new, unconfirmed Houthi claims of a strike on a Saudi oil field and an airport; pump prices refreshed from official US, EU and UK feeds.

entries.headline: Houthis claim fresh strikes on Saudi oil sites as Kpler data show Mideast exports matching pre-war levels
changes: Yemen's Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on Aramco's Yanbu site, the Shaybah oil field, and airports in Riyadh and Abha; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed the claims.

Kpler ship-tracking data put total Middle East oil flows, including Hormuz bypass routes via the Gulf of Oman, Fujairah and the Red Sea, at over 24.5 million barrels a day in the week to Oct 18 — edging above the pre-war baseline on this broader measure.
Brent crude eased to about $110.74/bbl after touching a five-month high near $111.50 on Oct 20; pump prices refreshed from official US, EU and UK feeds.
The IMO's confirmed toll in the Strait of Hormuz rose to 116 attacks and at least 24 deaths since the war began, up from 113 on Oct 14.

entries.headline: Iran's oil terminals sit idle for a ninth week as the US eases 'dark fleet' tanker sanctions
changes: Bloomberg reports no tankers have loaded at Kharg Island, Iran's main export terminal, since late August — the longest idle stretch of the war.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the US will let investors buy and refurbish sanctioned tankers to carry non-sanctioned crude, easing record Gulf-to-Asia freight rates.
A tugboat was damaged by projectiles northeast of Khor Fakkan, UAE; UKMTO logged 25 ships targeted in and around the Strait of Hormuz in the first two weeks of October, up from 18 in September.
A Qatari LNG cargo took a rare Red Sea route toward Europe as a skiff fired on another LNG tanker in the Gulf of Aden.
Brent rose to about $111.50/bbl; Russian Arctic oil exports to Asia already exceed all of last year's total.

entries.headline: Iran reiterates its Hormuz-reopening offer; Turkey to take diesel under the Russia-US deal
changes: Iran's foreign minister says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days of a US acceptance still stands.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards claim two more tankers hit mines in the strait itself (unverified; no independent confirmation).
Turkey's energy minister says Ankara will take some of the diesel Russia is supplying under the Trump-Putin deal.
Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones over the country's Black Sea waters, days after drone strikes on two chemical tankers near the Sulina Canal.
Brent eased to about $108/bbl; EU gas (TTF) set a fresh 2026 high near €90/MWh.

entries.headline: UKMTO logs more tanker attacks off Saudi Arabia; Vitol warns of a lasting ship-fuel shortage
changes: Two tankers struck northeast of al-Jubail, Saudi Arabia on Oct 16, outside the Strait of Hormuz; Iran separately claims they hit mines (unverified).
Vitol's Asia head says a global shortage of high-sulfur fuel oil for ships will persist even as crude flows through Hormuz rise.

entries.headline: UKMTO says most Hormuz tanker attacks go unreported; Iran evaded the blockade with LPG and jet fuel
changes: UKMTO's weekly overview said most ships struck near Hormuz don't report the attack to it, and counted only 42 AIS-tracked transits in the week to Oct 14 against the US military's claim of about 400

Reuters tracking data showed Iran has moved at least 4.1 million barrels of LPG and one jet-fuel cargo past the US naval blockade since mid-July, even as its crude exports hit zero in September for the first time since 2013
The IEA agreed to speed up roughly 100 million barrels of emergency oil releases, including over 20 million barrels of diesel, as the diesel shortage from the war risks lasting into 2027
Gulf-to-China supertanker freight rates eased about 8% from record highs as Middle East demand cooled
Brent rose to about $109.86/bbl and WTI to about $101.41/bbl

entries.headline: US military claims control of Hormuz; drones hit two more tankers off Romania
changes: US Central Command said the US and regional partners control the Strait of Hormuz, citing over 40 commercial transits in 24 hours; independent tracking (JMIC) put US-facilitated transits at only about 30 a day over Oct 11-14, roughly a fifth of the pre-war rate

The IMO put the confirmed toll in the strait since the war began at 113 incidents and at least 24 seafarer deaths as of Oct 14; JMIC separately logged 149 confirmed vessel incidents region-wide since March 1
Drones hit the tankers Wine Trader and Yara J off Romania's Black Sea coast on Oct 15; 7 of Wine Trader's crew are missing, and an unnamed NATO source said the drones were Russian-made

The Trump administration is weighing easing sanctions on 'shadow fleet' tankers that have carried Russian, Iranian or Venezuelan oil, to relieve record freight rates squeezing Gulf and US crude exports
Brent rose to about $105.91/bbl and TTF gas hit a fresh 2026 high near €87.80/MWh

entries.headline: Houthi strike hits Aramco's Dhahran HQ; two more ships sink in the Strait of Hormuz
changes: Houthi missiles and drones struck Saudi Aramco's Dhahran headquarters overnight Oct 13, sparking a fire Reuters sources described across several floors; Riyadh's airport stays closed through Oct 17 after this week's deadly strikes

The container ship GFS Pride sank in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 13 (21 crew safe) and the bulk carrier Cape Dao, struck in September, has now sunk too; Iran's naval-mine claim was disputed by a maritime security firm
US Central Command said it destroyed an Iranian-linked dhow in the Gulf of Oman on Oct 6, alleging it helped target US Navy ships
Drones hit two cargo ships off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast; one sank with 11 crew still missing
Trump said Russia would start releasing diesel to global markets before the US midterms; US senators and EU officials pushed back, and analysts doubted it would lower prices
Brent eased to about $104.63/bbl; AIS-tracked tanker traffic through Hormuz fell to just 0.6 ships a day, 99% below the pre-crisis baseline

entries.headline: Trump's Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' claim disputed as Saudi-Houthi fighting escalates
changes: Trump said Russia and Ukraine agreed to an immediate energy ceasefire; Zelensky called it news to him and said Russian drones hit a Ukrainian gas facility and five other energy targets hours later (unverified claims from both sides)

A Houthi strike on Riyadh's main airport over the weekend killed at least 13 people, the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in a decade; the Saudi-led coalition struck Houthi sites in Sanaa on Oct 13, including an empty fuel depot, and the Houthis threatened Aramco's Dhahran headquarters
Supertankers are turning away from the Fujairah transfer hub near the Strait of Hormuz as attacks continue, risking the shuttle-tanker system that bypasses Hormuz
Saudi Arabia is studying raising its East-West pipeline's capacity to 10 million barrels a day within 2-3 years
Brent rose to about $106.55/bbl and WTI to about $95.23/bbl

entries.headline: Hormuz attack toll for Oct 11 was six ships, not two, the highest single day of the war
changes: Delayed UKMTO and JMIC reports disclosed six vessels, five tankers and a container ship, were struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 11 — a fuller count than the single tanker reported at the time; JMIC raised its threat assessment for the strait to SEVERE
No injuries were reported in any of the six incidents, and no group claimed responsibility
Brent crude eased to about $104.64/bbl; EU TTF gas hit a new 2026 high of about €85.86/MWh

entries.headline: More tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz; Iran calls US reopening response 'insufficient'
changes: A fully laden VLCC (GEM NO.2) was struck by a projectile off the UAE coast on Oct 9, outside the usual Hormuz attack cluster, and two more unnamed tankers were hit by projectiles inside the strait on Oct 10 and 11; crews were reported safe in all three incidents
Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the US response to Iran's seven conditions for reopening the strait was 'insufficient' and that Tehran would stop responding through the current channel
Brent crude rose to about $105.60/bbl, up roughly 2.7% from a week earlier

entries.headline: Status added for eleven facilities that were shown as operating normally
changes: Eleven facilities whose notes described damage or shutdowns now have a sourced status: Abqaiq processing plant, Jazan refinery, Primorsk and Ust-Luga ports and the Moscow refinery (damaged); SAMREF refinery, Ras al-Ju'aymah terminal, Mesaieed Industrial City, Mina Abdullah refinery, Shah gas field and Basra Oil Terminal (reduced)

Several earlier notes were out of date: Primorsk and Ust-Luga resumed loading in late March and early April, Basra's exports recovered to about 2.6 million b/d in September, and Shah's production was rising again by May

Abqaiq: the damage from the Jul 27 drone strike is now recorded on the processing plant, where it happened; the Abqaiq oil field no longer carries that status, and the three related events link to the plant

Abqaiq oil field: removed a '~1 million b/d processing capacity' figure that matched neither the field nor the plant. The plant's capacity is about 7 million b/d; the field's own output was put near 400,000 b/d in the early 2010s, and no current figure is available
Haifa's Bazan refinery was checked and found to be running near capacity, so it has no status entry; its note now says so
Capacities recorded with sources for Jazan, SAMREF, Mina Abdullah, Primorsk, Ust-Luga, the Moscow refinery (about 11 million tonnes a year, not 12) and Bazan
Where no report could be found after a given month, the status entry says so

entries.headline: Gulf of Mexico shut-ins ease as Isaias weakens; DOE taps reserve for Exxon, BP
changes: Hurricane Isaias weakened to post-tropical after landfall near Destin, Fla.; Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins eased to about 69% of output, down from a 71.5% peak
DOE authorized an emergency 4-million-barrel Strategic Petroleum Reserve exchange (2 million barrels each to ExxonMobil and BP) to support Gulf Coast refineries
CENTCOM said it disabled a tanker leaving an Iranian port and gave a running tally of blockade enforcement since July; the figures are the US military's own and unverified

Correction: the Turkish Straits returned to normal shipping in early August after a brief Dardanelles permit halt — this site had left that status as unresolved for two months; it has now been cleared
Houthi media said they repelled a Yemeni-government push to retake Mayyun Island on Oct 10, contradicting the Oct 9 claim that the island had been retaken; both sides' claims remain unverified

entries.headline: Corrections: chokepoint oil flows, Habshan–Fujairah capacity, Tuapse status and a tanker attack location
changes: Chokepoint descriptions now give the same pre-crisis oil flows as the What-if model, with their period and source: Hormuz 19.9 million b/d (IEA, 2025); Malacca 23.2, Suez 4.9, Bab el-Mandeb 4.2 and the Turkish Straits 3.7 million b/d (EIA, first half of 2025). The descriptions previously carried older figures (21, 16, 5–6, 6–7 and 3.5)
Habshan–Fujairah pipeline: capacity recorded as 1.5 million b/d nameplate, with the reported 1.7–1.8 million b/d running rate noted; the What-if model's note now says the same
Tuapse refinery: added a status entry (damaged since Apr 16 after four drone strikes in two weeks; no restart reported, status after May not verified) and its capacity (about 240,000 b/d)
Oct 7 tanker attack (Acers): map position moved to 51 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, as UKMTO reported; it had been placed just off the coast

entries.headline: Trump announces Russia-US diesel deal as Hormuz flows fall and Gulf of Mexico shut-ins reach 71.5%
changes: Trump announced Russia would supply diesel to US and global markets in tranches, and that Treasury would temporarily ease sanctions on Russia's energy sector to allow it; the Kremlin confirmed the call but gave no tonnage, and no diesel has been delivered yet
Kpler data showed Hormuz crude exports falling to about 8.5 million b/d (about 40% below pre-war) in the week to Oct 7, down from 13.2 million b/d (77% of baseline) the week before
US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins ahead of Hurricane Isaias climbed further to about 71.5% of output, from 63% a day earlier

Iran's IRGC said it struck an LPG tanker in the strait for taking an 'unauthorized' route; the Saudi-led coalition said it struck 136 more Houthi targets and claimed Yemeni forces had also retaken Mayyun Island near Bab el-Mandeb (both unverified)
Ukraine said drones struck Gazprom Neft's Omsk refinery, Russia's largest, for a second time since July

entries.headline: Oil eases on Trump's no-strike pledge as Gulf of Mexico shut-ins deepen to 63%
changes: Brent and WTI eased 1-1.5% after Trump said the US will not attack Iran before November's midterm elections
US Gulf of Mexico oil shut-ins ahead of Hurricane Isaias deepened to 63% of output, from 25% a day earlier
A chemical tanker was struck off Qatar, west of the usual Strait of Hormuz attack cluster, and Reuters reported Iran plans to widen threats against ships on 'unauthorized' routes
Saudi Arabia's energy minister said the East-West pipeline reached 5.8 million b/d (83% of capacity); Saudi Aramco is in talks to formalize long-term Hormuz-bypass shuttle contracts
Gulf-to-Asia supertanker freight rates hit a record near $1.4 million/day as the Hormuz shuttle system strains vessel supply

entries.headline: Hurricane shuts in a quarter of Gulf of Mexico oil output as Hormuz attacks hit a record week
changes: Brent and WTI jumped about 5% to roughly $105 and $93 as Hurricane Isaias approached the US Gulf Coast
Shell and Chevron shut in production and evacuated staff from Gulf of Mexico platforms; US regulators put the shut-in at about 25% of Gulf oil output
The UN's IMO recorded 9 tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in the week of Sep 28-Oct 5, the most of any week since the war began
Vortexa and Kpler data showed non-Iranian Gulf oil flows averaged 81% of their pre-war rate in September, while Iran's own exports stayed near zero

entries.headline: Oil rebounds as Hormuz attacks continue and Iran's exports near zero
changes: Brent and WTI rebounded to about $101.9 and $89.98, snapping three days of declines
A dozen seafarers were injured when the tanker On Peace was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 5, UKMTO and India's government said
Tracking group UANI, corroborated by Bloomberg, found Iran loaded no crude at all in September and exports have fallen to about 50,000 b/d from 966,000 b/d in July
Yemeni government forces claimed full control of Bab el-Mandeb under 'Operation Yemen Dawn'; Houthi media denied it and it remains unconfirmed
Qatar positioned a dozen empty LNG carriers in the Gulf, signalling a possible export boost

entries.headline: Oil prices fall to multi-week lows as East-West pipeline ramps up
changes: Brent and WTI fell for a third straight session ($97.95 and $87.32), WTI's lowest since early September
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is now moving close to 6 million b/d, over 80% of capacity, up from about half in late September
Updated pump prices, benchmark prices and the situation summary

entries.headline: Seventh Hormuz tanker strike logged; Yemeni forces claim Bab el-Mandeb gains
changes: UKMTO reported the Liberian-flagged tanker Lipsi struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Oct 4, leaving it disabled; crew safe, no environmental impact
Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said they seized Dhubab district near the Bab el-Mandeb strait from the Houthis; Houthi media denied the claim and it remains unconfirmed
Brent ticked up to $102.80, WTI held near $90.63, and TTF gas eased slightly to €74.43/MWh

entries.headline: New data dashboard, with free downloads
changes: A new dashboard brings every key figure together: ship traffic through each chokepoint, pump prices in 36 markets, oil and gas benchmarks, facility status, the event log and how much oil each chokepoint carries
Charts are interactive: compare pump prices across countries, filter events by week and kind, and search all 176 mapped assets
Six datasets can be downloaded as CSV or JSON, rebuilt on every update and free to reuse under CC BY 4.0

entries.headline: Added Riyadh Refinery after a fire and a Houthi strike claim
changes: Added Saudi Aramco's Riyadh Refinery (126 kb/d, fed by the East-West Pipeline) as a tracked facility
Reuters and AFP witnesses saw a fire there on Oct 3; Yemen's Houthis claimed a missile-and-drone strike, which Saudi authorities and Aramco have not confirmed

entries.headline: UKMTO logs a sixth Hormuz tanker attack; Saudi Arabia reportedly readies Houthi offensive
changes: UKMTO's delayed disclosures now put at six the number of vessels struck in the Strait of Hormuz since 28 September
Officials told reporters Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemeni-led ground offensive, backed by Saudi air power, to retake Bab el-Mandeb from the Houthis; no timeline is confirmed
The UK sanctioned eight more Russian shadow-fleet and LNG-export vessels, including five named LNG carriers
Checked Bab el-Mandeb's width and flow figures against current sources; no change needed
Refreshed FX rates used for pump-price conversions

entries.headline: US sanctions Iran's carmakers and railways; pressure grows on Europe's diesel reserves
changes: US Treasury's "Operation Economic Outcast" sanctioned Iran's two biggest automakers, its state railway and a major freight operator, plus foreign parts suppliers, targeting the road and rail routes Iran has used to move oil and goods overland since the Hormuz blockade
The US pressed Germany and France to release more diesel reserves, saying both have drawn down only a fraction of what they pledged in March's coordinated IEA stock release
Brent held near $100 and WTI eased to $89.36 on 2 Oct amid the diesel-reserve dispute
Checked Suez Canal's capacity and trade-share figures against current sources; no change needed
Refreshed FX rates used for pump-price conversions

entries.headline: Banks see Mideast oil flows near pre-war levels; more Hormuz tanker attacks surface
changes: JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs estimate Middle East crude shipments have recovered close to pre-war volumes (Hormuz flows near 13 million b/d), though both banks say this reflects adaptation to risk rather than improved safety
UKMTO disclosed three more Hormuz tanker attacks via delayed reports, highlighting growing gaps in incident reporting
Trump denied offering Iran sanctions relief; Iranian officials said reopening the strait would follow a seven-day countdown after any deal
Brent rose to $99.74/bbl and WTI to $91.45/bbl on 1 Oct as markets weighed the conflicting signals
Refreshed EU pump prices and FX rates from official feeds

entries.headline: Hormuz flows hit 13.2 mb/d as Saudi Red Sea exports rebound; Brent, WTI pull back
changes: Kpler ship-tracking data and satellite imagery show a 'major operational recovery' at Saudi Arabia's Yanbu export terminal, with Strait of Hormuz oil flows averaging 13.2 million b/d (about 77% of Kpler's pre-war baseline) over the week to 29 Sep
Brent fell 2.6% and WTI 3.5% on 29 Sep as the recovery weighed on prices, before easing further into 30 Sep
Updated Brent, WTI, TTF, JKM and Henry Hub benchmark prices
Refreshed pump prices from official EIA/EU/UK feeds

entries.headline: East-West pipeline ramps to 3.5 mb/d; Hormuz tanker traffic picks up
changes: Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline has recovered to roughly 3.5 million b/d, about half its capacity, after last month's drone strikes; full resumption is expected in about six weeks

Kpler ship-tracking data show Strait of Hormuz crude exports recovering to a 7.4 million b/d September average, with Gulf-wide exports at their highest since the war began — though the strait remains formally closed to normal traffic
Updated Brent, WTI, TTF, JKM and Henry Hub benchmark prices
Refreshed pump prices from official EIA/EU/UK feeds

entries.headline: Saudi Arabia's 60-million-barrel Sohar workaround, and Trump-Iran talks may resume this week
changes: New: Saudi Arabia has sold ~60 million barrels of Ras Tanura crude for ship-to-ship transfer at Sohar, Oman, to offset the Yanbu/East-West pipeline outage — the relay is now near capacity
New: Trump told Axios he expects US-Iran talks, mediated by Qatar, to resume as soon as this week, a day after rejecting Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
Updated the Ras Tanura terminal and Strait of Hormuz situation summaries

entries.headline: Updates now on X: @StratEnergyMap
changes: Significant developments, a daily digest and weekly charts are posted automatically, with the same sourcing rules as the map
Posts about items that need human review only go out once they're approved; Bluesky is coming next

entries.headline: Clearer map style
changes: New 'paper and slate' basemap: warm land and slate-blue water, so coastlines and chokepoints read clearly
Crisper markers with white outlines, lighter oil and gas field shading, and stronger shipping routes

entries.headline: Collapsible panels and a better phone layout
changes: Hide a side panel with the « or » button in its header; a labelled tab at the edge of the map brings it back, and the map remembers your choice
On phones the feed is a bottom sheet: tap or swipe the handle to expand or minimise it, and the map opens full-screen
Selecting an item centres it in the visible part of the map

entries.headline: Answer pages for every chokepoint, major facility and pump-price series
changes: 130 readable pages generated from the map's data, e.g. 'Is the Strait of Hormuz open?' and diesel prices in each EU country
Events archive with an RSS feed
Pages refresh automatically with each daily update

entries.headline: New permanent address: strategicenergymap.org
changes: The map moves to strategicenergymap.org; old links redirect automatically

entries.headline: About page, credits, link previews and public changelog
changes: New About & methods page explaining sources, the sourcing rule, the update agent and the what-if model
Link previews for LinkedIn, Slack and messaging apps
Embeddable map view (add ?embed=1 to the URL)
Privacy-friendly, cookie-free visitor counts

entries.headline: Sourcing rule for parties to the conflicts
changes: Claims by governments that are parties to the conflicts (including the US) are attributed and marked unverified unless independently verified
Ship transits and flows through Hormuz and other contested waters now come only from independent trackers, named in the text
Hormuz what-if model rebased on the IEA's February 2026 factsheet (Kpler data)

entries.headline: Catch-up: February–September 2026
changes: 63 sourced events covering the Iran war and Hormuz closure, the Red Sea and the Black Sea
17 facilities marked as not operating normally
13 newly relevant facilities added (e.g. Abqaiq plant, Jazan, SAMREF, Basra terminal, Primorsk, Ust-Luga)
Benchmark prices as of 25 September

entries.headline: Version 2: Americas, live data, pump prices and what-if mode
changes: Americas added: US Gulf Coast LNG, Permian, Guyana, Brazil pre-salt, Venezuela, Canadian oil sands, Panama Canal
Live chokepoint ship traffic from IMF PortWatch
Weekly pump prices for the US, EU and UK from official sources
Chokepoint closure what-if mode
Daily automated update agent with a sourcing policy and validation checks

entries.headline: First version published
changes: Map of pipelines, fields, refineries, ports and chokepoints across Europe, the Middle East and Asia, with geopolitical context
